answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, a decentralized economy of AI agents can employ a mechanism known as "Voting Lanterns." Each agent is assigned a unique lantern, and a threshold number of lanterns must be gathered before a proposal can be deemed valid. This creates a "terrace" effect, where an attacker must accumulate an excessive number of lanterns to achieve a majority. Furthermore, a bridge-like consensus protocol can be employed to prevent a single attacker from rapidly accumulating lanterns, thereby securing the network against fake-identity attacks.
